one_month_reasoning: The one scheduled event in the window is Q3 2026 results on 2026-10-14 (guidance: sales EUR 11-12B, GM 55-57%; consensus EPS about $12.54 on about $13.2B revenue, which is the top half of the guide). The operating print should be fine: H1 sales were EUR 18.1B, so the EUR 43-45B full-year guide implies EUR 25-27B in H2. The stock reaction is the open question. ASML fell after raising guidance in July, and it has already rallied about 12.5% from the 2026-09-14 AI-pacing low of $1,606.66 to $1,808 on UBS and JPM support, so much of the relief is priced in. What will move it is the first color on 2027 and the 2028 order intake (JPM says most new EUV orders are now for 2028). Two other things could land in the window. NDAA conference headlines on the MATCH Act would skew down, but the conferenced bill is not expected before about 2026-11-22, so a final outcome inside the window is unlikely. Hyperscaler Q3 capex updates in late October skew slightly up, since Alphabet has already guided 2027 capex up 'significantly'. These skews roughly cancel. I stay close to symmetric around spot with a 1-month sigma of about 13.5% (46%/3.5, nudged up slightly for earnings day). The new evidence did not justify a directional tilt, so the ladder is essentially unchanged from my capped round-1 version.

fair_value.method: Blend of (a) 28x NTM EPS at Oct-2027 of about $60 (25% FY2027 EUR 49.5, 75% FY2028 EUR 55, at 1.1245 USD/EUR) = $1,688 (50%); (b) cycle-normalized 2027E EPS of $47.3 (a 15% haircut to $55.7) x the 15-year average P/E of 34.4x = $1,628 (30%); and (c) a 3.0% FCF yield on about $21B of 2027E FCF over 378M shares = $1,852 (20%). The blended fair value is about $1,700, roughly 6% below spot.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: NTM EPS at Oct-2027 = 0.25 x FY27 EUR 49.5 + 0.75 x FY28 EUR 55 = EUR 53.6, x 1.1245 = $60.3; multiple 28x

inputs_detail.value: EUR 44B (midpoint of EUR 43-45B); H1 actual EUR 18.1B (Q1 8.8 + Q2 9.3)

inputs_detail.derivation: H1 EPS about EUR 14.8 (Q2 basic EUR 7.59 plus Q1 about EUR 7.3), so H2 needs about EUR 23.5, which fits a ~35% net margin on EUR 25-27B of H2 sales.

Low-NA EUV capacity goes from about 65 to about 85 units (+30%), DUV immersion capacity +30%, and 2027 is nearly fully covered. I trim that to +18% because Zeiss EUV optics capacity is reported up only 20-25% in 2027, China (14-16% of system sales in 2026) is at MATCH Act risk, and service growth is slower than systems. This is down from my round-1 +22% (EUR 53.5B), and it sits close to one aggregator's EUR 50.6B consensus.

The implied H2-2026 net margin is about 35% at a 55-57% GM. EUV price increases (TSMC reportedly pushing back) and opex leverage add about 1 pt. Round 1 used 34%, which the consensus 2026 EPS now shows was too low.
Q2 net income EUR 2.918B / basic EPS EUR 7.59 = 384M; EUR 1.1B a quarter of buybacks retires about 0.6-0.7M shares a quarter.
EUR 52B x 36% / 378M = EUR 49.5. That is slightly below the post-July aggregator consensus of about EUR 51.7 (snippet only) and below Erste's $61.40, which is the skeptic haircut.

Bernstein is at EUR 67 for 2028, which it says is 35% above consensus (so July consensus was about EUR 50). Most new EUV orders are now for 2028 delivery and ASML is studying 110+ units. I take +11%, between July consensus and Bernstein, because 2028 is still 'under review' and optics capacity is the binding constraint.

Today's NTM P/E is about 34x (about EUR 47 NTM EPS). NTM EV/EBITDA is 23.6x vs a 10-year mean of 24.9x (Torre), so the multiple is not stretched on that measure. The 15-year average P/E is 34.4x and the 5-year median trailing P/E is 39x. I apply 28x, about 6 turns below today, because in Oct-2027 the market will be pricing 2028-29, the window where semicap upcycles have historically ended.

methods.name: other
methods.inputs: Cycle-normalized EPS: 2027E $55.7 x 0.85 = $47.3 x 34.4x (15-year average P/E)

inputs_detail.derivation: Semicap upcycles have historically ended in 30-50% EPS declines. ASML's backlog and its 5,500-tool installed base cushion that, but 43% of Q2 system sales went to Korea (memory, the most cyclical buyer), and hyperscaler capex now outruns their cash flow (only 1 of 6 is forecast FCF-positive in 2027). I keep about a third to a half of a typical drawdown.

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: 2027E FCF ~EUR 18.7B (~$21.0B), about equal to net income; a 3.0% yield gives ~$700B of equity; / 378M shares

inputs_detail.derivation: Set equal to 2027E net income of EUR 18.7B (EUR 52B x 36%), with customer prepayments on the growing 2027-28 backlog offsetting expansion capex.
The current FCF yield is 1.8% vs a historical 2.6% (Torre). I use 3.0%, above the historical average, to allow for peak-cycle risk at the horizon.

bear.story: The MATCH Act is enacted in the year-end NDAA with DUV immersion and servicing bans on SMIC, Huawei, Hua Hong, CXMT and YMTC. The 150-day ally clock means unilateral FDPR controls by mid-2027, taking out most of the remaining China business (14-16% of system sales plus the service base; BofA's full-ban case was -14-15% of revenue when China was ~29%). At the same time, hyperscalers that already depend on external financing pace 2027-28 capex, memory makers (43% of Q2 system sales) digest their HBM build, and 2028 EUV orders get pushed out. 2028 EPS stalls around $50 and the market re-rates ASML as a cyclical at ~22x.

base.story: 2027 delivers about +18% revenue and ~$56 EPS on the EUV capacity ramp, and 2028 is guided to modest double-digit growth (~$62). The MATCH Act passes in some form, but with a long ally-coordination window and service carve-outs, so the 2027 hit is a few percent. The multiple compresses from ~34x NTM to ~29-30x, so earnings growth roughly offsets de-rating and the stock ends near today's price.

bull.story: AI and DRAM demand pull the 2028 plan up to 110+ EUV units, Zeiss keeps pace, price increases stick, GM reaches 58-60%, and the MATCH Act is stripped or diluted in conference (Dutch lobbying, Trump-Xi détente). 2028 EPS reaches about $70 (toward Bernstein's EUR 67) at ~36x.

thesis_break_reason: Below about $1,200 (about -34%, near a 1-sigma annual move, about 22x 2027E EPS of $55.7 and well under the $1,606 September panic low), the market would be pricing an earnings decline, not just multiple compression on growing earnings. Most likely causes: customers pushed out 2027/2028 EUV slots (bookings collapsing, 2028 capacity plans withdrawn), or the MATCH Act became law with an immediate servicing ban on the China installed base. Either would break the fundamental thesis rather than reflect ordinary volatility. Unchanged from round 1.

Durability of AI and memory capex into 2028. Hyperscaler capex now exceeds their cash flow and relies on external financing, and Korean memory makers were 43% of Q2 system sales, which concentrates the exposure on the most cyclical buyers.

Customer pushback on EUV price increases (TSMC) vs margin upside.
reasoning: Skeptic lane, continuation run with a restored search budget (about 25 more searches plus page reads). I set out to verify the round-1 bear vectors. (1) MATCH Act: verified and re-scoped. It rides the NDAA, which the House passed on 2026-09-10 but the Senate did not before the 09-22 recess. Conference is expected by about 11-22 and final passage by year-end. The bill targets named fabs (SMIC, Huawei, Hua Hong, CXMT, YMTC) and gives allies 150 days before unilateral FDPR controls, with a waiver. China has already fallen to 14% of Q2 system sales (16% in H1), so a ban hits 2027 less than BofA's full-ban scenario (-14-15% revenue, built when China was ~29%) implied. It also makes the ban more likely to pass (44-0 committee vote) and harder for Dutch lobbying to stop. Net: lower severity, similar probability. (2) Credit: no stress. Moody's A1 moved to positive outlook on 2026-07-23, and S&P is A+. (3) Litigation: the 2024 securities class action survived most of the motion to dismiss on 2026-03-27 and is in discovery; immaterial to value. (4) Insiders: only February 2026 sales of identical small amounts by the CEO and CFO (consistent with vesting/tax), one board purchase, nothing in the last 3 months. Short interest is about 0.4% of float. No red flag. (5) Cycle: the strongest new bear evidence. Hyperscaler capex outruns their FCF and needs external financing, and memory (Korea 43% of Q2 system sales) concentrates exposure. Against that, Alphabet guided 2027 capex up significantly, SK hynix has an $8B EUV commitment through 2027, and JPM says most new EUV orders are for 2028 delivery. (6) Valuation: today's NTM P/E is about 34x (higher than the ~31x I assumed in round 1), but NTM EV/EBITDA of 23.6x is near its 10-year mean of 24.9x, so the 'extreme multiple' bear case is weaker than trailing P/E suggests. Consensus 2026 EPS of EUR 38.3 showed my round-1 34% net margin was too low, so I lifted margins to 36% and cut the 2027 revenue growth assumption to +18% for optics and China. 2027 EPS rose slightly to $55.7, and 2028 to $61.8. Fair value moves from $1,640 to about $1,700 (6% below spot). The scenario mean is about $1,812, roughly spot. For the 12-month ladder I set the median at about $1,780 and a lognormal sigma of about 42% (below the 46% realized vol because of backlog visibility), with a modestly fattened left tail for the policy/cycle combination. That shifts the middle of the ladder up 1-2 points vs round 1. Remaining gaps: several sell-side/aggregator pages (Seeking Alpha, Morningstar, chartmill, valueinvesting, CNBC, SCMP, Digitimes) returned 403 or paywalls, so 2027 consensus EPS (about EUR 51.7) comes from search snippets only. I found no Polymarket or Kalshi market on the MATCH Act or chip export controls. Alpha Vantage estimate and insider endpoints were rate-limited.
